assertion.name: Reverse T3 in the newborn period

assertion.name: Annual ophthalmologic examination and EEG surveillance
assertion.description:
The recommended ongoing surveillance rather than a diagnostic test at presentation: annual ophthalmological examination, EEG, and anticonvulsant drug-level monitoring.
The ophthalmological arm has a specific, gene-specific evidence base beyond the GeneReviews recommendation. In a prospectively and uniformly examined cutis laxa cohort, reduced corrected visual acuity was found only in the ATP6V0A2 patients, and all four had corneal tomographic abnormalities - so corneal imaging, not just acuity, is the informative examination.

assertion.name: Combined transferrin and apolipoprotein C-III isoelectric focusing
assertion.description:
The first-line screen, and the step that selects ATP6V0A2 out of the genetically heterogeneous cutis laxa group before sequencing. Transferrin focusing detects the N-linked limb and apolipoprotein C-III focusing the O-linked one; it is the combination that points at a Golgi-homeostasis defect rather than an endoplasmic-reticulum one or a single-enzyme CDG.
Every ATP6V0A2 patient in the prospective neurometabolic cutis laxa cohort had abnormal glycosylation, so a normal result argues against the gene more strongly than an abnormal one argues for it.
assertion.markers: Type II transferrin isoform profile on serum transferrin isoelectric focusing, together with an abnormal apolipoprotein C-III isoform profile detecting the mucin-type O-linked limb.
assertion.results: A combined N- and O-linked abnormality. Either limb alone points elsewhere: an isolated transferrin abnormality is compatible with many CDGs, and it is the pairing that localises the defect to Golgi homeostasis.
assertion.notes: `Diagnosis.markers` is a single free-text string with no ontology binding, so a two-analyte test cannot be represented as two grounded markers here - both are named in one sentence instead. The HP term for the transferrin finding, HP:0012301, is carried on the corresponding `phenotypes` and `biochemical` entries, which is where it can be validated.

selected_evidence.snippet: All patients with ATP6V0A2 defects had abnormal glycosylation.

assertion.description: Serologic testing for VZV-specific IgM (acute infection) and IgG (prior immunity) antibodies. IgM appears within a few days of rash onset and persists for weeks. IgG seroconversion or four-fold rise in paired sera confirms recent infection. IgG testing is primarily used to assess immune status rather than diagnose acute disease.

selected_evidence.snippet: The early production of VZV-specific IgG or IgM antibodies did not correlate with the severity of the clinical infection

assertion.name: VZV PCR
assertion.description: Real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of vesicle fluid, crusts, or saliva is the gold standard for laboratory confirmation. VZV DNA can also be detected in blood (T-lymphocyte-associated viremia) from approximately 5 days before to 4 days after rash onset.

selected_evidence.snippet: Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) can be detected in the blood from approximately 5 days before to 4 days after varicella.

assertion.name: Clinical diagnosis
assertion.description: Varicella is primarily diagnosed clinically based on the characteristic appearance of the rash with simultaneous lesions in multiple stages (macules, papules, vesicles, crusts) in a centripetal distribution. In vaccinated individuals, modified varicella may present atypically with fewer, predominantly maculopapular lesions.

selected_evidence.snippet: VZV infections are ubiquitous and highly contagious, and diagnosis is mostly based on the assessment of signs and symptoms.

assertion.name: Cerebrospinal fluid cystatin C measurement
assertion.description: Markedly reduced CSF cystatin C was one of the earliest available measures in living carriers. It has been superseded by molecular testing and is not specific on its own.
assertion.results: CSF cystatin C is markedly diminished in HCCAA patients.

assertion.name: Brain computed tomography
assertion.description: CT imaging is used to confirm intracranial hemorrhage when new neurological symptoms develop in a known carrier.
assertion.results: Demonstrates intracranial hemorrhage underlying new neurological symptoms.

selected_evidence.snippet: A computed tomography (CT) scan of the brain was acquired if new onset of neurological symptoms occurred.

assertion.name: CST3 molecular genetic testing
assertion.description: Detection of the CST3 L68Q founder variant is definitive. Because the mutation abolishes an AluI site, RFLP analysis historically provided a simple and accurate assay, and it supports presymptomatic and prenatal diagnosis.
assertion.results: Presence of the CST3 L68Q allele establishes the diagnosis of HCCAA.

selected_evidence.snippet: Since the HCCAA-causing mutation abolishes an AluI restriction site in the cystatin C gene, analysis of this AluI restriction fragment-length polymorphism (RFLP) enables simple and accurate molecular diagnosis of HCCAA.

assertion.name: Skin biopsy for cystatin C immunoreactivity
assertion.description: Because skin and CNS pathogenesis correspond closely, quantifying cystatin C immunoreactivity in skin biopsies provides an accessible measure of disease progression, and it was used as the primary biomarker readout in the NAC trial.
assertion.results: Cystatin C immunoreactivity in skin, initially confined to the dermal-epidermal basement membrane, tracks disease stage.
